verifiedFacts.claim: Agent SDK provides Claude Code's agent loop, built-in tools (read/edit files, run commands) and permissions
Client SDK: you write the tool loop yourself or use the beta tool runner (tools still team-authored)
Code execution tool runs in Anthropic's sandboxed container, not on the local repository

issues: Minor: stem phrase 'built-in file-editing and shell tools' closely mirrors option A, but this is the tested requirement, not an unfair cue.

verifiedFacts.claim: Thinking blocks must be passed back complete and unmodified with the tool_use block during a tool-use turn, including redacted_thinking
Signature must be passed exactly; modified thinking blocks are rejected with 400
tool_choice any/tool errors with manual extended thinking
Python SDK retries 2 times by default with short exponential backoff (5 outer x 3 = 15 attempts matches stem)
SDK retries connection errors, 408, 409, 429, >=500; 400 invalid_request_error not retryable
_request_id property on responses; request-id header on responses
Default timeout is 10 minutes (5s timeout would break normal generations)

issues: Minor: option B does not itself say 'stop retrying 400s', but removing the outer loop does that implicitly since the SDK does not retry 400.
suggestedFix: Optional: in B say 'Remove the outer loop and tune max_retries...' to make the 400 consequence explicit.

verifiedFacts.claim: Batches complete within 24h, most within 1 hour (unsuitable when a user waits minutes)
Prompt caching and Message Batches discounts stack
Batch requests processed concurrently in any order; cache hits best-effort (30-98%); consider 1-hour cache for batches
max_tokens: 0 is rejected inside a Message Batches request
Cache entry only available after first response begins; wait for first response before parallel requests

issues: Option E says 'with one request' without specifying it is a synchronous Messages API request outside the batch; a careful reader might wonder whether it is a separate one-request batch.
Docs do not explicitly state that a cache written by a synchronous request is hit by later batch requests (same-workspace cache scope makes it reasonable).
suggestedFix: E: 'First write the shared prefix with one synchronous Messages API request using a 1-hour cache TTL, then submit the batch once it completes.'

verifiedFacts.claim: claude --resume <name> resumes a named session and restores full history including tool calls and results
--fork-session creates a copy of the conversation with a new session ID (history copied, not refreshed)
Claude reads files fresh on each tool call

issues: Minor: Claude Code may surface external file modifications itself in some cases; A remains wrong as worded ('restored Read results already show the merged code') and B is safe regardless.

verifiedFacts.claim: Tool descriptions and server instructions significantly affect whether Claude finds and uses MCP tools (tool search)
Scope precedence is local > project > user for duplicate definitions; no 'loaded before built-in tools' behavior
MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS controls output size limit (default 25,000), not tool selection
Refining tool descriptions improves tool selection; describe as to a new hire
context: fork runs the skill in a subagent of the agent type, with SKILL.md as the task
Built-in Explore and Plan skip CLAUDE.md and git status; a forked skill with agent: Explore sees only SKILL.md and the agent's system prompt

issues: Option C embeds its own justification ('since the Explore agent skips CLAUDE.md'), which slightly stands out vs. D's parallel justification; acceptable since D's justification is equally assertive and false.

verifiedFacts.claim: Batches support tool use, multi-turn conversations; almost any Messages request can be batched (C is false)
Batch requests processed asynchronously; results available when all complete or after 24h (no mid-request injection of tool results)

issues: Minor: a multi-round batch design (batch returns tool_use, app runs lookup, follow-up batch) is also viable in principle but is not offered, so A is uniquely defensible among options.
